assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data turned intergenerational mobility into a measurable, place-specific object. It reshaped empirical public and labour economics and the policy debate on opportunity, and it came with credible quasi-experimental designs on neighbourhood effects.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is central to nearly every component. Hendren is the key figure on causal place effects and on welfare measurement. Friedman is central to the data-construction and tax-record work. Katz has important earlier and complementary contributions, such as Moving to Opportunity, but is left off the three names to respect the cap. Credit within this large team is contestable.
assessment.maturity: The core results date from roughly 2014 to 2022 and have been widely replicated and extended. The area is highly influential, though some long-run causal claims are still being tested.
uncertainties: The three-laureate cap forces a choice among Chetty, Hendren, Friedman and Katz.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for more evidence on long-run causal neighbourhood effects.
The concentration of credit in Chetty may crowd out others, or may dominate the prize in another framing, for example the B037 tax work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints that amplify and propagate shocks are foundational for macro-finance. The Kiyotaki-Moore credit-cycles mechanism and the financial accelerator underpin the modern analysis of financial crises, balance-sheet channels and unconventional policy.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the credit-cycle mechanism. Gertler is central to the financial accelerator and its macro-finance applications, but shares that credit with Bernanke, who was already honoured in 2022 for banks and financial crises. Gilchrist is an important empirical and quantitative contributor but secondary.
assessment.maturity: The work is decades old and has been validated by the 2007-09 crisis and a large literature. Timing is not a constraint.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize to Bernanke, Diamond and Dybvig may weigh against it.
Whether Gertler or Gilchrist should be included alongside Kiyotaki and Moore is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence on local labour markets reshaped how economists think about automation, trade, adjustment and inequality. The work has had large academic and policy influence.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure across both strands. Hanson and Dorn are co-authors on the trade-shock work, and Dorn also on polarization. Katz has key skill-premium contributions, and the task framework also has major theoretical contributors, such as Acemoglu, who are not on this ballot entry. The credit structure is therefore not clean.
assessment.maturity: The papers date from 2003 to 2016 and the literature has since grown. The long-run persistence of the China shock and the evidence on automation are still being studied.
uncertainties: Task-model theory credit sits partly outside this list.
Some debate over how far the China-shock estimates generalize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities is the workhorse of monetary policy analysis in central banks. It is a major, enduring intellectual contribution.
assessment.attribution: Credit is highly diffuse: Calvo for the pricing model, Woodford and Gali for the canonical synthesis and policy analysis, Taylor for the rule, Christiano and Eichenbaum for medium-scale estimation, Smets for estimated DSGE models, and Gertler for the early NK literature. Any three-person selection leaves out many equally defensible names.
assessment.maturity: The work is fully mature and has been tested over decades, including the post-2008 and post-2021 inflation episodes.
uncertainties: The three-name cap makes a clean attribution hard.
Prior macro prizes already cover related ground, such as Lucas, Sargent and Sims, and Kydland and Prescott.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fairness, reciprocity and inequity aversion are well formalized and experimentally validated, and they inform contract theory, labour markets and public goods provision. The Fehr-Schmidt model became the standard formal tool for social preferences.
assessment.attribution: Fehr is the most clearly central figure. Schmidt co-authored the formal inequity-aversion model, and Falk contributed to field and experimental evidence and later work on preferences. Credit overlaps with other social-preference authors, such as Rabin and Bolton-Ockenfels, who are not on this entry.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the late 1990s and 2000s and has been extensively replicated and extended. Some heterogeneity and external-validity questions remain.
uncertainties: Behavioural economics has recently been recognized, with Kahneman and Thaler, which may reduce room for another prize.
Debate over how well lab fairness findings carry over to market settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HANK models integrate household heterogeneity and wealth distributions into monetary and fiscal transmission analysis. This changed how macroeconomists think about marginal propensities to consume and policy channels, and it connects to computational advances.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll and Violante are the natural trio for the HANK synthesis and the two-asset framework. The approach builds on earlier heterogeneous-agent work, such as Aiyagari, Huggett, Krusell-Smith and Bewley, which dilutes credit.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from about 2016 to 2018 and are still evolving. Policy relevance is high, but the long-run empirical record is shorter than for other candidates.
uncertainties: A relatively young literature whose lasting influence is not yet fully settled.
Because I work in adjacent macroeconomics, I may be overweighting the field's perceived importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed the analysis of the gains from trade and spawned a large empirical literature using firm-level data. It is a major extension of the new trade theory recognized in 2008.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the central originator. Helpman has major complementary contributions on heterogeneous firms in trade, and Redding on quantitative spatial and trade models. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are significant contributors not on this entry.
assessment.maturity: Melitz (2003) has had two decades of testing. The core insight is well established, and it has been refined by quantitative work questioning how much heterogeneity matters for welfare.
uncertainties: Credit is incomplete because Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are missing from this entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design give a general framework for how a sender can shape beliefs through information structures, with applications to markets, regulation and communication. It is conceptually elegant and influential in theory.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow wrote the foundational persuasion paper. Morris and Bergemann developed the broader information-design and robust-mechanism agenda. A three-person selection leaves out Bergemann, who is arguably equally central to the broader field.
assessment.maturity: The foundational paper dates from 2011 and the field is growing. Empirical and policy influence is still developing compared with other candidates.
uncertainties: Relatively young, with limited empirical validation so far.
The three-name cap forces an unclear split between persuasion and the broader information-design agenda.
